title: A radial ionization bound limits electron-scattering screens at the ASASSN-14ko orbital scale
abstract: Can directly illuminated ionized gas hide the soft X-ray source at the ASASSN-14ko recurrence radius? We integrate the ionization density limit along the radial ray. The column bound holds for any density profile and any outer radius under the stated direct-illumination criterion. The published soft-excess fraction limit requires Thomson depth of at least 7.77. For a 108.44-day circular scale and a black-hole mass of 10^7.86 solar masses, a screen with xi at least 10^4 erg cm/s throughout needs ionizing luminosity of at least 2.63 x 10^44 erg/s. If its outer radius is twice its inner radius, the required luminosity is 5.26 x 10^44 erg/s. Under a test ceiling of 2 x 10^44 erg/s, the inner edge must lie inside 192 gravitational radii, below the orbital scale of 252. Increasing radial depth cannot evade the integral limit. This is a conditional constraint on one screen branch, not an exclusion of occultation or proof of an intrinsic shutdown. Ionization thresholds and the luminosity ceiling are assumptions, not new measurements. Cold opaque covering, a smaller radius, collisionally ionized gas and trapped radiation remain possible. We supply the derivation, code, sensitivity figures, synthetic results and a verified retrieval recipe for the cited scalar input.
